title: What if the whole Earth froze over? 🧊
subject: ice
description:
Could anything survive a frozen planet? 👇

What would happen if Earth froze from pole to pole? It already did: during the Sturtian 'Snowball Earth' ice age, 717 to 660 million years ago, ice reached the equator for 57 million years.

Sources: University of Sydney via ScienceDaily, "What turned Earth into a giant snowball 700 million years ago?" (Geology, 2024); Live Science, "Snowball Earth: When the Blue Planet Went White" (2019)

scenes.text: If Earth froze, you could ski across the equator.
Temperatures would average minus 50 degrees Celsius.
White ice reflects sunlight, so the colder it gets, the faster it cools.
From 717 to 660 million years ago, it really happened, for 57 million years.
University of Sydney researchers blame volcanic carbon dioxide falling below 200 parts per million, under half today's level.
Volcanoes likely ended it too, piling up gas until Earth flipped into a hothouse within a few centuries.
